simulators.name: Simulators
simulators.no_xcode: Xcode command line tools are not available, so simulators can't be listed.
simulators.shared_image: {{.Count}} runtime entries share one disk image. Deleting this one deletes the image for all of them.
simulators.newest_runtime: {{.Runtime}} is the newest runtime of its platform. Xcode needs it to run simulators.
simulators.not_deletable: macOS marks this runtime as not deletable.
simulators.device_booted: The simulator {{.Device}} is running on this version. Shut it down first.
simulators.runtime_missing: Its OS runtime is not found right now. It may come back after a restart; deleting would lose the simulator and its data.
simulators.runtimes.title: Simulator runtimes
simulators.runtimes.what: Disk images with an iOS, watchOS, tvOS or visionOS version that simulators run on. Each one is 7–9 GB.
simulators.runtimes.why: Older versions are only needed to test on that exact OS version. They can be downloaded again in Xcode › Settings › Components.
simulators.runtimes.after: Simulators on this version stop working until you download it again.
simulators.devices.title: Simulators
simulators.devices.what: Simulated iPhones, iPads and other devices with the apps and data installed on them.
simulators.devices.why: A simulator can be created again in a minute. Running simulators can't be selected.
simulators.devices.after: Apps installed on the simulator and their data are lost. Build and run your app again to reinstall it.
simulators.dyld_cache.title: Simulator dyld cache
simulators.dyld_cache.what: Prepared system libraries that make simulators start faster, one set per runtime.
simulators.dyld_cache.why: macOS rebuilds the cache the next time a simulator of that version starts. Caches of deleted runtimes are useless.
simulators.dyld_cache.after: The first start of a simulator takes a few minutes longer. Deleting asks for the administrator password.
